## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

ProfileRepository.updateCorrectionFactor — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/profile/ProfileRepository.kt

## Trigger

Called from EndOfRaceViewModel.init, with the last retained blended factor — observed. Called from ProfileSyncPushService.applyProfile, with the incoming payload's correctionFactor — observed.

## Today

The four other profile updaters — updateHrMaxBpm, updateZoneThreshold, updateExpectedDistanceM, updateLongPressMs — validate their value in ProfileRepositoryImpl (core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/profile/ProfileRepositoryImpl.kt) and return Result.failure, leaving the stored value unchanged, when the value falls outside a fixed range. updateCorrectionFactor writes unconditionally and always returns Result.success(Unit), on both its interface contract and its ProfileRepositoryImpl implementation. EndOfRaceViewModel.init calls it with retainedFactor.factor, the blend of the newly measured factor (0.6 weight) and the previous stored factor (0.4 weight, CorrectionFactorCalculator.compute in core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sensor/CorrectionFactorCalculator.kt). Only the measured half of that blend is bounded, to 0.70..1.40 (TRUSTED_RANGE); the blended result and the previous factor it is built from are never checked. ProfileSyncPushService.applyProfile (core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sync/ProfileSyncPushService.kt) calls updateCorrectionFactor with the incoming payload's value the same way it calls the other four updaters, but — unlike them — that call can never fail and refuse the value. RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.markSegment reads profile.correctionFactor as previousFactor for the next blend (core-domain-consuming code in app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt) with no guard on what it read.

## Expected

updateCorrectionFactor validates its value against a fixed range the way the other four updaters do, refusing it and leaving the stored value unchanged when it falls outside — in both the interface's documented contract and ProfileRepositoryImpl. With that guard in place, a call from EndOfRaceViewModel.init carrying an out-of-range blended factor is refused, and a call from ProfileSyncPushService.applyProfile carrying an out-of-range incoming value is refused the same way an out-of-range hrMaxBpm, zoneThreshold, expectedDistanceM or longPressMs already is — applyProfile already treats updateCorrectionFactor's Result the same as the other four's, so no change is needed there. Because the previous factor is only ever written through this guarded path, a value later read as previousFactor by RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.markSegment is always within range, closing the self-feeding corruption without a separate guard at the read site.
